title: Apply for a club liquor licence
summary: A club liquor licence allows a registered club to sell alcohol to members and guests for consumption on and off the premises, and may also allow the operation of gaming machines.
intro:
A club liquor licence allows a registered club to sell alcohol to members and guests, for consumption on and off the premises. The licence also allows the operation of gaming machines, subject to separate approval.

For up-to-date liquor licence guidelines, resources and tools visit Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing.

If you have questions or feedback about liquor licensing contact Liquor & Gaming NSW.
who_can_apply: The applicant must be a corporation.
what_you_need: A OneGov account or MyServiceNSW Account
A floor plan showing the boundaries proposed for the licensed area
The names and birthdates of all directors and officeholders
An appointment of manager notice (if applicable)
A copy of your development approval or consent (if applicable)
A completed Statement of Risks and Potential Effects (SoRPE)
A copy of the club's constitution
A current Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) extract
A gaming plan of management (if applicable)
A declaration by the proposed club secretary (if applicable)

how_to_steps.text: Log in or create an account.
Follow the prompts to complete your application.

more_info.text: Some liquor licence applications require you to notify stakeholders and the local community about your application once it has been submitted.
Find out more about notification requirements at Liquor & Gaming NSW.

Conditions apply to NSW liquor licences. Some conditions apply automatically depending on the type of premises. Other conditions may be imposed on a licence by Liquor & Gaming NSW or the Independent Liquor & Gaming Authority.
Where there are conditions that may be applied, you can include the conditions form with your application. It may help reduce application processing time.
Find out more about licence conditions at Liquor & Gaming NSW.

Authorisations and exemptions can help you customise your on-premises licence to suit your needs. See the Liquor & Gaming NSW website for more information about club licences authorisations and exemptions.

faqs.q: Where can I find up-to-date guidelines for liquor licences?
faqs.a: Visit the Liquor & Gaming NSW liquor licensing page for resources and tools.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for a club liquor licence?
faqs.a: The applicant must be a corporation.

faqs.q: What is required to apply for a club liquor licence?
faqs.a: You need items such as a OneGov or MyServiceNSW Account, a floor plan, and the club's constitution.
